faq.a: Munther is associated with the Arabic form مُنْذِر, whose core sense is munther; warner, one who warns.

faq.q: What is the origin of Munther?
faq.a: Munther is associated with Arabic. Munther is Arabic مُنْذِر (Mundhir), the active participle of أَنْذَرَ, meaning 'warner'.
Yes — the underlying form مُنْذِر is Arabic.
Munther can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Munther should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root ن ذ ر is Quranic (warning), but Mundhir is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Munther mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Munther is rendered منذر and carries the sense منذر، ڈرانے والا.

faq.q: What does Munther mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Munther is rendered منذر and carries the sense منذر، هشداردهنده.
A romanized syllable approximation is mun-ther. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Munther?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Munther, munther. Script forms are منذر, مُنْذِر, मुंज़िर.

faq.q: Is Munther a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
